# Dwarf Galaxies: Small But Mighty

Though our Milky Way galaxy spans 100,000 light-years and contains hundreds of billions of stars, the universe's most common galaxies are actually cosmic minnows called dwarf galaxies—just one-tenth the size with only a few billion stars—yet the Hubble Space Telescope reveals they pack a surprising punch. These tiny galactic powerhouses, like NGC 4449 shown here, are mysteriously missing more oxygen than scientists expected, suggesting that stellar explosions and powerful winds are violently scattering the heavy elements that form stars, planets, and ultimately life itself across the cosmos.
